name: Aoki Lock to Back Control
description: A back take after Aoki Lock Control needs a separate rear torso attachment; the original control alone does not establish hooks, a seatbelt or completed back control.
summary: A back take after Aoki Lock Control needs a separate rear torso attachment; the original control alone does not establish hooks, a seatbelt or completed back control.
overview:
The initial Aoki Lock Control configuration must be identified before considering Back Control. The captured limb is the foot and lower leg. This is distinct from an omoplata-style shoulder trap and from a bent-knee calf slicer. Either player can become the foot-lock attacker during an entanglement exchange. The reviewed instruction does not establish a direct Aoki Lock Control-to-Back Control connection. Release the original lock safely and establish the destination's own prerequisites; do not treat these checkpoints as a demonstrated continuous entry.

The opposing foot is turned outward and enclosed near the armpit, upper arm, and forearm. Rotational foot locks can injure the ankle or knee before pain provides useful warning. Use cooperative capture-and-release practice, no spinning escapes, and the event's actual division rules. Open the original connection before either partner turns, rises or changes the captured limb.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Instructional sources: [Stephan Kesting and Rob Biernacki — the Aoki lock](https://www.grapplearts.com/the-step-by-step-aoki-lock/); [IBJJF — current rule resources](https://ibjjf.com/books-videos).

The initial Aoki configuration is a leg entanglement around a captured foot and hip. Release the rotational foot capture before changing sides; a back take still requires a new rear torso attachment.

flashcards.question: Aoki Lock to Back Control (attacker): What does the initial grip enclose?
flashcards.answer: The opposing foot is turned outward and enclosed near the armpit, upper arm, and forearm.
flashcards.answer_line: An outward-turned foot beside the armpit

plausible: A straight foot with only Achilles contact
An inward-turned foot beside the armpit
trap: A turned-out foot held only at the toes

flashcards.question: Aoki Lock to Back Control (attacker): Why unload the foot before changing sides?
flashcards.answer: Rotational foot locks can injure the ankle or knee before pain provides useful warning. Use cooperative capture-and-release practice, no spinning escapes, and the event's actual division rules.
flashcards.answer_line: Hip movement can rotate the captured ankle and knee

plausible: The foot grip only compresses calf muscle
The hip can turn independently of the held foot
trap: A seated turn leaves the knee unloaded

flashcards.question: Aoki Lock to Back Control (attacker): What must open before turning toward the back?
flashcards.answer: Open the original connection before either partner turns, rises or changes the captured limb.
flashcards.answer_line: The foot enclosure and restraining leg connection

plausible: Only a hand while the armpit keeps the foot fixed
Only the hip connection while the foot stays clamped
trap: The leg connection after the turn has begun

flashcards.question: Aoki Lock to Back Control (attacker): After release, what contact begins a separate back take?
flashcards.answer: Establish a separate chest-to-back connection before reaching for hooks or a seatbelt.

plausible: Your chest beside their back with a gap
Your chest against the front of their shoulder
trap: Your chest against their hip with shoulders detached

flashcards.question: Aoki Lock to Back Control (attacker): What secures both shoulder and hip lines from behind?
flashcards.answer: Use controlled upper-body and leg attachment while preserving neck alignment.
flashcards.answer_line: Attachment around both the torso and hips

plausible: Hooks while the chest stays far away
A seatbelt with no control of the hips
trap: A waist grip while your chest drifts off the back

flashcards.question: Aoki Lock to Back Control (attacker): What shows rear control still needs work?
flashcards.answer: Confirm that the opponent cannot simply turn to face you before considering a back attack.
flashcards.answer_line: The opponent can turn their chest toward you

plausible: Your chest follows their back as they move
Your legs contain their hip line
trap: Their chest stays facing away inside your attachment

flashcards.question: Aoki Lock to Back Control (attacker): What lower-body restraint belongs to the initial Aoki setup?
flashcards.answer: The initial configuration manages a foot and its hip; it does not already contain rear hooks.
flashcards.answer_line: Legs managing the captured leg's hip

plausible: Feet touching the ankle with the hip free
Knees beside the thigh without enclosing the leg
trap: Crossed ankles detached from the opponent's hip

plausible: The heel grip also fixes the opponent's shoulder line

flashcards.question: Aoki Lock to Back Control (attacker): The partner starts turning with the foot fixed. What opens?
flashcards.answer: Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.
flashcards.answer_line: Both the arm enclosure and hip restraint

plausible: Only the hand clasp, leaving the instep clamped

flashcards.question: Aoki Lock to Back Control (attacker): Where should the forearm support the initial capture?
flashcards.answer: The forearm supports the heel/Achilles area while the upper arm encloses the instep.
flashcards.answer_line: Beneath the heel and Achilles region

plausible: High beneath the calf, clear of the heel
Across the top of the instep
trap: Under the toes with the heel outside

flashcards.question: Aoki Lock to Back Control (defender): After foot release, how do you deny rear torso access?
flashcards.answer: Keep the shoulders facing the opponent before a seatbelt closes.
flashcards.answer_line: Keep your shoulders facing the opponent

plausible: Turn your shoulders away while leaving hips behind
Reach backward while leaving the chest turned away
trap: Face the hips while leaving your shoulders turned away

flashcards.question: Aoki Lock to Back Control (defender): After release, how do you address an arm nearing your neck?
flashcards.answer: Hand fight any arm approaching the neck while maintaining a stable base.
flashcards.answer_line: Intercept that arm with your hands

plausible: Grip only the wrist resting at your waist
Peel a hip hook before checking the neck arm
trap: Tuck the chin and allow the hands to connect

flashcards.question: Aoki Lock to Back Control (defender): After release, where is your elbow as you turn to face?
flashcards.answer: A compact elbow beside the ribs and knee protects the arm and closes space for rear access.
flashcards.answer_line: Close to the ribs and returning knee

plausible: Flared outward above the approaching forearm
Flared away from the knee toward the mat
trap: Extended forward past the returning knee

flashcards.question: Aoki Lock to Back Control (defender): After the lock opens, what barrier helps recover facing guard?
flashcards.answer: Bring the knee inside behind a frame and keep the elbow connected as you face the opponent.
flashcards.answer_line: An inside knee joined to the near elbow

plausible: Both knees pointed away from the opponent
An elbow frame with the knee outside their hip
trap: An inside knee with the elbow lifted away

flashcards.question: Aoki Lock to Back Control (defender): Your torso can turn but the foot is fixed. What comes first?
flashcards.answer: Wait for a trapped foot or arm to be released before changing direction.
flashcards.answer_line: Release of the foot and hip restraints

plausible: Turning the shoulders before moving the hips
Freeing only the hip while retaining the foot clamp
trap: Turning the knee before clearing the heel
